title: Asset
description: An asset is a configuration record, not a code path. Mirrors `Asset` in src/domain/asset.ts: an AssetDefinition (slug, symbol, decimals, class — what is true everywhere) materialised onto one tenant's books with an `id`. Nothing in the engine knows what gold is, which is exactly why it can settle something else. Unknown keys are refused unless prefixed `x-`.

id.description: Supplied at the edge by materialize(); no default. Entries reference this value in `assetId`. In production it is the ObjectId of a row in the consumer's assets collection — never the slug.

slug.description: Stable machine name, lower-case kebab, e.g. 'flashy-gold', 'wheat'. The pattern is SLUG_PATTERN in src/domain/registry.ts (tests/schema.test.mjs fails if they drift); defineAsset() refuses anything else because it appears in URLs and every published registry.

symbol.description: Ticker shown to people, e.g. 'FG', 'WHT'. 2–8 upper-case alphanumerics starting with a letter — SYMBOL_PATTERN in src/domain/registry.ts.

decimals.description: How many decimal places this asset settles to (0 to MAX_DECIMALS in src/domain/registry.ts). Commodities are usually 0. Precision is enforced at the boundary: fromDecimal(0.5, 0) throws rather than rounds. Flashy Gold is 2 — it was declared as 4 in one of four places once, and the wrong one was the published one.

class.description: Mirrors `AssetClass` in src/domain/asset.ts; tests/schema.test.mjs fails if the two lists drift. SKILL_XP is not transferable: status settled with the money ledger's discipline, never convertible to it.

tenantId.description: Which network's books this asset belongs to.
